title: Ordering Food at a Restaurant
description: Learn to order food and interact with waiters
objectives: Order food politely (I would like... / Can I have...?)
Ask questions about the menu (What is...? / Do you have...?)
Ask for the check (Can I have the check?)
Understand basic menu items and restaurant vocabulary

phrases: Can I have the check, please?
target_language.grammar_pattern:
I would like + noun
Can I have + noun?
What is + noun?

Examples:
- I would like a burger
- Can I have water?
- What is the soup of the day?
- For here, please

grammar_patterns.label: Requesting items
examples: Can I have the check, please?

grammar_patterns.label: Asking about the menu
examples: What is the soup of the day?

story.context: You are at a restaurant. The waiter comes to take your order.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Good afternoon! Welcome to Joe's Diner. Are you ready to order?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes. Can I have a hamburger, please?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Sure! For here or to go?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Great. What would you like to drink?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll bring that right out.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Excuse me. Can I have the check, please?

drills.title: Drill 1: I would like...
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct food or drink
drills.your_turn: Now order your favorite food using 'I would like...', out loud, and record it

drills.title: Drill 2: Can I have...
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct item
drills.your_turn: Now ask for something at a restaurant using 'Can I have...', out loud, and record it

drills.title: Drill 3: Questions about menu
drills.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word

prompts.sentence: What is the ___ of the day?

examples: What is the soup of the day?
drills.your_turn: Now ask a question about a menu item, out loud, and record it

listening.question: Listen: What does the customer order?
listening.explanation: The customer says 'I would like a hamburger'

listening.question: Listen: Is it for here or to go?
Listen: What drink does the person want?
listening.explanation: The person says 'I would like water'

speaking.title: Task 1: Order food
speaking.instruction: Record yourself ordering: a hamburger, french fries, and water. Use 'I would like' or 'Can I have'.
speaking.example: I would like a hamburger. Can I have french fries? And water, please.

speaking.title: Task 2: Restaurant conversation
speaking.instruction: Record a full restaurant conversation. Order food, answer if it's for here or to go, and ask for the check.
speaking.example:
Waiter: Are you ready to order?
You: Yes. I would like a burger.
Waiter: For here or to go?
You: For here.
(later)
You: Can I have the check, please?

writing.title: Task 1: Write your order
writing.instruction: You are at a restaurant. Write what you would order: a main dish, a side, and a drink. Use 'I would like...'
writing.example: I would like a chicken sandwich. I would like a salad. I would like iced tea.

writing.title: Task 2: Write a restaurant conversation
writing.instruction: Write a conversation (10-12 lines) at a restaurant. Include: greeting, ordering food and drink, answering questions, and asking for the check.
writing.example:
Waiter: Hello! Are you ready to order?
You: Yes. I would like a burger.
Waiter: What would you like to drink?
You: Water, please.
Waiter: For here or to go?
You: For here.
Waiter: Anything else?
You: No, that's all.
Waiter: I'll bring that right out.
(later)
You: Can I have the check?
Waiter: Here you go.
You: Thank you!

sections.title: Polite requests: Would like vs Want
sections.question: Which sounds more polite in a restaurant?
sections.explanation: 'I would like' is more polite than 'I want'. In restaurants and formal situations, we use 'I would like' or 'Can I have' to sound polite.

sections.title: For here vs To go
examples: For here, please (eat in the restaurant)
To go, please (take the food with you)
sections.question: What do these mean?
sections.explanation: 'For here' means you will eat in the restaurant. 'To go' (or 'takeout') means you will take the food with you to eat somewhere else.

sections.title: That's all vs Anything else
examples: Waiter: Anything else? (Do you want more?)
You: No, that's all. (I don't want anything more)
You: Yes, can I have water? (I want something more)
sections.question: What does the waiter mean by 'Anything else?'
sections.explanation: 'Anything else?' means 'Do you want anything more?' You can say 'No, that's all' if you're finished ordering, or tell them what else you want.

quiz.question: What is the MOST polite way to order food?
quiz.explanation: 'I would like a burger' is the most polite way to order.

quiz.question: The waiter asks 'For here or to go?' What are they asking?
options: Do you want it now or later?
Will you eat here or take it with you?
Do you want big or small?
Do you want it hot or cold?
quiz.explanation: They're asking if you will eat in the restaurant (for here) or take the food with you (to go).

quiz.question: You want the check. What do you say?
options: Can I have the check, please?
quiz.explanation: 'Can I have the check, please?' is the most polite and complete way to ask.

quiz.question: The waiter asks 'Anything else?' You're finished ordering. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'No, that's all. Thank you.' is complete and polite.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: I ___ like a salad.
quiz.explanation: We say 'I would like a salad'. 'Would like' is polite.

quiz.question: You want to know what 'chicken alfredo' is. What do you ask?
quiz.explanation: 'What is chicken alfredo?' is the correct question.

quiz.question: You want to eat in the restaurant. The waiter asks 'For here or to go?' You say:
quiz.explanation: 'For here, please' is the complete and polite answer.

quiz.question: Which sentence is the correct way to order food at a restaurant?
options: I'll have the grilled chicken, please.
quiz.explanation: 'I'll have the grilled chicken, please' is polite and natural — it's the standard way to order food in a U.S. restaurant. 'I want' and 'Give me' are too direct and can sound rude. Always use 'please' when ordering.

quiz.question: Write an 8-line conversation where you order a pizza, soda, and ask for the check.
quiz.explanation: Your conversation should include: the waiter asking if you're ready, you ordering food and drink, the waiter confirming, and you asking for the check.

quiz.question: What is your favorite food? How would you order it in a restaurant? Write 2-3 sentences.
quiz.explanation: Practice ordering food you actually like. This makes it more meaningful and easier to remember.
